_note: Release config for THIS repo, read by bin/promote-cards-by-token AND (since card#8174) by bin/release-pr-guard.py, which composes the expected release-branch name as `release/` + `tag_format` — so tag_format now has TWO readers and changing it moves both. DELIBERATELY MINIMAL: it carries only keys something in this repo actually READS — `tag_format` (the mover's last-release-tag glob; the guard's branch-name authority) and `promote` (board correlation + the two stage-id sets). Do NOT 'complete' it with main_branch/dev_branch/version_file/version_regex/artifacts: nothing here reads them today, README.md already owns the branch model, and a second copy would be free to drift with nothing binding it. Add a key when a consumer for it lands, not before. WORKED CASE: release-pr-guard needed the release branch name and did NOT add `main_branch` — it derives it from `on.push.branches` in .github/workflows/auto-tag-version.yml, the trigger that IS the operational definition of the branch a push tags. A need for a key is not yet a reason for one; look for the statement that already exists first. SECURITY: `promote.api_base` is where KANBAN_WRITEBACK_TOKEN is sent, and this file is PR-editable — so the committed value is a HOST-SCRUBBED PLACEHOLDER. The real base arrives at run time from the repo variable KANBAN_API_BASE (out-of-band from this file), and the mover's host guard fail-closes against the repo variable KANBAN_EXPECTED_HOST before any token leaves the runner. Treat ANY edit to api_base as a credential-scope change and review it as one.
